memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "To purify the house he is to take two birds and some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop. He shall kill one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot. Then he is to take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn and the live bird, dip them into the blood of the dead bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times." - Lev 14:49-51 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same ceremony that cleansed a person now cleanses a house. Two birds, cedar, scarlet yarn, hyssop, blood, fresh water, seven sprinklings.

God does not have one method for people and another for their dwellings. The same blood cleanses both.

That says something about how far God's redemption reaches. He is not content to save individuals and leave everything they touch untouched. His purpose extends to homes, to families, to the places where life is lived.

Joshua understood this. Standing before the nation, he said: as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD (Josh 24:15). Not just me. My household. Paul told a terrified jailer in Philippi to believe in the Lord Jesus, and that night the man and his whole family were baptised (Acts 16:31-34).

Hyssop appears here, and it is worth noting where else it appears. David prayed, cleanse me with hyssop, and I will be clean (Ps 51:7). And at the cross, when Jesus said "I am thirsty," they lifted the sponge to Him on a stalk of hyssop (John 19:29).

The blood that cleanses your heart is the same blood that can transform your home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your faith stop at your own heart, or shape your household?
2. What would it mean to consecrate your home to God this week?
3. What one change would make your home a place where Christ is honoured?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, be honoured not only in my heart but in my home. Cleanse the atmosphere of this house, and let those who live here know Your presence. Amen.
